description: FIRST FEATURES-SCOPE MIRROR GOLDEN (mirror v2, docs/design/mirror-semantics.md) — the chain whose three legitimate readings proved that NO implicit rule can be right (§1), authored with the intent stated instead of inferred. A 40 x 40 mm plate extruded 20 mm; a single r4 through-bore drilled by the HOLE feature at (10,20) on the +Z face; an 8 x 8 x 5 BOSS extruded on a datum at z=20 over x in [30,38], y in [30,38]; a YZ-parallel datum at x=20 (the plate's x-midplane); then a MIRROR whose `scope` is `{kind: features, features: [hole, boss]}`. The v2 mechanism reflects each SELECTED feature's RECORDED RIGID TOOL and re-applies THAT feature's own boolean, in TREE order: the hole's bore tool reflects to x=30 and is CUT (-320pi), then the boss prism reflects to x in [2,10] and is FUSED (+320). The SAME tree with a bare `mirror {plane}` (scope `body`, which is also what every pre-v2 persisted mirror normalises to) still returns 30309.3807 — the hole mirrored, the boss NOT duplicated — and that is deliberate, not a shortfall: 30629.3807 from an implicit mirror would require GUESSING that the user meant hole-and-boss rather than hole, which §1 proves cannot be guessed correctly for all chains (`test_composition_matrix.py::test_cm1_mirror_keeps_the_hole_across_an_intervening_feature` locks BOTH spellings). Locks: the scope union + its tree-ordered application (an array order of [boss, hole] must give this same body), the per-feature tool store widened to additive verbs (§6.2), `reflect_tools` + `cut_reflected_tools` + `fuse_reflected_tools`, and (via the parametrized gates) in-process + interpreter-restart byte-determinism and STEP round-trip. The `body`-scope mirror goldens (mirror-hole-feature-plate-40x40x20, mirror-cut-clearing-plane-block-40x40x20, mirror-triangle-prism-2x) are UNCHANGED and byte-identical — verified GLB-sha256-equal against the pre-v2 kernel over all 39 goldens.
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED analytic values, not recorded harness output (geometry-gates skill: a golden recorded from buggy output enshrines the bug). Plate: outer square x,y in [0,40] on XY (4 lines, no constraints -> zero residual, planegcs returns input positions bitwise), extruded 20 mm along +Z = the box [0,40] x [0,40] x [0,20], volume 40*40*20 = 32000 mm^3.
seed hole: a diameter-8 (r4) through-all bore at (10,20) on the +Z face, removing pi*4^2*20 = 320pi = 1005.3096 mm^3. Strictly interior (x=10 > r4, y=20 centred).

seed boss: a datum parallel to XY slid +20 mm along +Z (the plate's top plane), an 8 x 8 square sketched on it over x in [30,38], y in [30,38], extruded 5 mm = +8*8*5 = 320 mm^3 over z in [20,25]. Pre-mirror volume = 32000 - 320pi + 320 = 31314.6904 mm^3.
mirror plane: a datum parallel to YZ (normal +X) slid +20 mm -> the plane x=20, the plate's x-midplane.

mirror, TREE order (the array order in model.json is [hole, boss]; §8.1 makes the applied order the EVALUATION order either way): (1) the HOLE's recorded bore tool reflects about x=20 from x=10 to x=30 and is CUT -> -320pi; (2) the BOSS's recorded prism reflects from x in [30,38] to x in [2,10] (y and z unchanged) and is FUSED -> +320.

disjointness (what makes the deltas exactly additive): the two bores at (10,20) and (30,20) are 20 mm apart with r4 each (12 mm clearance) and strictly interior; the two boss footprints x in [30,38] and x in [2,10] are strictly interior to [0,40]; each boss spans y in [30,38] while each bore spans y in [16,24], so no boss overlaps a bore. The reflected boss sits ON the plate's top face, so the fuse keeps ONE connected solid.

volume = 32000 - 2*(pi*4^2*20) + 2*(8*8*5) = 32000 - 640pi + 640 = 30629.380701702532 mm^3. The `body`-scope answer for this same chain is 30309.380701702525 (one boss), so this value FAILS on the v1 semantic by exactly 320 mm^3.

surface_area: bottom cap 1600 - 2*pi*4^2 (pierced by both bores); top cap 1600 - 2*pi*4^2 - 2*8^2 (pierced by both bores AND covered by both boss footprints); 2 boss tops 2*8^2; 2 x 4 boss walls 2*(4*8*5); 4 plate side walls 4*(40*20); 2 bore cylinders 2*(2*pi*4*20). Total = (1600 - 32pi) + (1600 - 32pi - 128) + 128 + 320 + 3200 + 320pi = 6720 + 256pi = 7524.247719318987 mm^2.
bounding_box = [0,0,0]..[40,40,25]: the bores are strictly interior; the bosses rise 5 mm above the 20 mm plate.

topology: 18 faces = 1 bottom cap + 1 plate top cap + 4 plate side walls + 2 bore cylinders + 2 x (4 boss walls + 1 boss top). 42 edges = 4 bottom rect + 4 top rect + 4 vertical plate corners + 2 x (2 bore circles + 1 cylinder seam) + 2 x (4 footprint + 4 boss-top + 4 boss-vertical). 1 shell (the bosses fuse onto the plate). The v1 `body`-scope answer for this chain is 13 faces / 30 edges, so the counts discriminate too.

mesh (linear 0.1 mm / angular default, isRelative=False): each full bore circle discretizes to 2*ceil(2*pi/0.1) = 126 segments (r4 keeps linear deflection non-binding). 2 periodic bore cylinders = 2*((126+1)*2 nodes, 126*2 tris) = 508 vertices / 504 triangles. Bottom cap: 4 + 2*126 = 256 boundary nodes with 2 holes -> 256 vertices, 256 - 2 + 2*2 = 258 triangles. Plate top cap: 4 + 2*126 + 2*4 = 264 boundary nodes with 4 holes -> 264 vertices, 264 - 2 + 2*4 = 270 triangles. 4 plate side walls = 4*(4, 2) = 16 vertices / 8 triangles. Each boss = 4 walls + 1 top = 5*(4, 2) = 20 vertices / 10 triangles; two bosses = 40 / 20. Totals = 508 + 256 + 264 + 16 + 40 = 1084 vertices and 504 + 258 + 270 + 8 + 20 = 1060 triangles (per-face faceted normals, no vertex sharing across faces).

GLB byte size is deliberately NOT pinned: it is asserted deterministic (byte-identical) by the runner within one kernel version, but pinning the absolute size would break on every glTF-writer upgrade without geometric meaning.
tolerance_rationale: CURVED-CUT + REFLECTION tolerance, the SAME reviewed tier the existing mirror-of-a-bore golden (mirror-hole-feature-plate-40x40x20) and pattern-cut-6hole-boltcircle-60x60x10 carry — reused verbatim, no new epsilon (RESEARCH §9 / docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md's two tiers). The reflection is an EXACT handedness-reversing isometry, but the reflected cylindrical tool is boolean-CUT through curved walls whose GProp volume/surface use Gauss quadrature, so a small residual compounds through the cut. Measured deviations vs the analytic values (2026-07-29, build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9, planegcs): volume |30629.380701702532 - 30629.380701702525| ~ 7.3e-12, surface_area ~ 1.1e-12, centroid.x 4e-15 (0.0 to display precision), centroid.y/.z ~ 1.6e-14, AABB bounds exactly 0.0. The 1e-8 ceiling covers the worst measured residual with ~1400x headroom for libm/BLAS/platform variation across CI hosts while staying 10x TIGHTER than the standing planar 1e-7 kernel bound. Topology and mesh counts carry NO tolerance (exact-match). Loosening this bound requires a reviewed kernel-level justification recorded here and in docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md.
